# Draft:Battle of the Five Roads

----
The Battle of the Five Roads - refers to the war between Mongolia and China that took place between 1912 and 1915. The Mongolian side aimed to liberate Inner Mongolia from Chinese troops and annex it, while the Chinese side aimed not only to not lose Inner Mongolia, but also to destroy the Bogd Khanate of Mongolia and seize its territory. This war is known in China as the "Ox Year Riot", and since the Chinese military operations during the war were largely unsuccessful and often defeated, it is not studied in depth, and the sources are characterized by falsely recording their defeats as victories.
During the Battle of the Five Roads, the Bogd Khan's government divided its troops into three routes to protect the Khovd region and liberate Western Mongolia or Xinjiang from China. There is almost no research on this, and there is little information in the sources. The Mongol-Chinese war that took place separately from the Battle of the Five Roads is called the Battle of the Three Roads.
The six assemblies of Inner Mongolia, including Zuu Ud, Zost, Jirêm, Shiliin Gol, Ulaancâv, and Ikh Zuu, the governors of the left and right banks of the Tumed River in Hohkh, the governors of the Khar River, the Ueldi governors, Alshaa, Ar Khorchin, the left bank of the Ili River, and the khoshu of Tarvagatai aimag, expressed their gratitude and joy, and sent troops from the capital area to liberate Inner Mongolia from Chinese oppression. Barga of Hulunbuy, 36 of the 49 khoshu of the six assemblies of Inner Mongolia joined Mongolia, and 24 khoshu of the Khar Lake, 8 khoshu of the Tsakhar River, 16 khoshu of the Ili River, and 16 khoshu of the Tarvagatai aimag officially joined. By decree of Bogd Khan, in July 1913, a special department was established to administer the affairs of the eastern region, and the wise and generous Khamba Galsandashi, a member of the Tsetsen Khan aimag, was appointed as its head.
